bull_bear.body:
- Decades of experience executing large-scale ICT and e-Governance projects for Government of Rajasthan departments, positioning the Company for future Government/institutional digital-education and public-digital-infrastructure initiatives
- Empanelment of subsidiary's JAN TV with DIPR (Government of Rajasthan) and CBC (Government of India, formerly DAVP) for Government advertising assignments, and multi-platform distribution (Tata Play, Airtel Digital TV, JioTV, MX Player, Dailyhunt, YouTube Live)
- Existing land bank enabling diversification into new consumer segments and industry verticals (hospitality, cold-chain/food processing) alongside the core ICT business
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competitive pressure — The technology industry sees intense competition from domestic and global players across software services, digital transformation, e-Governance, cloud computing, AI and managed services; sustained innovation, service quality, execution capability and cost efficiency are critical to maintaining market position.
- Talent acquisition and retention — Strong sector-wide demand for skilled professionals in AI, cloud, cybersecurity, data analytics and digital engineering makes availability/retention of qualified talent a key challenge that may push up employee costs.
- Rapid technological change / obsolescence — The accelerating pace of technological advancement raises the risk of technology obsolescence; competitiveness depends on continuously upgrading capabilities and aligning offerings with evolving customer requirements and industry trends.
- Foreign exchange exposure — A part of revenue is derived from overseas operations and international clients (including US execution facilities), so fluctuations in the Rupee against major global currencies may impact revenue, margins and competitiveness.
- Regulatory and policy risk — The business is influenced by Government policies on IT, digital governance, education, taxation and public procurement; changes in laws, Government spending priorities, fiscal incentives or policy frameworks (Central or State) could affect operations and growth. The generic risk list flagged in the MD&A also cites political instability and legal-framework risk.
- Client concentration — Client concentration is explicitly flagged among the risks and concerns continuously monitored by the Board and senior management, given the Company's reliance on large Government/institutional counterparties for its ICT and e-Governance project revenue.
- Fixed-price contract execution risk — The Company flags time- and cost-overruns on fixed-price contracts as a monitored risk, relevant given its multi-year, fixed-value Government ICT/school-infrastructure project contracts.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company operates across e-governance projects, ICT education initiatives, software design and development, electronic media (television broadcasting via subsidiary CSL Infomedia Private Limited under JAN TV/JAN TV Plus), IT and media training, learning solutions, and wind power generation, with a recently completed diversification into hospitality through Hotel Ranavilas Palace, Jaipur. It primarily executes large-scale ICT/e-Governance and school-computerisation projects for Government of Rajasthan departments and Rajasthan Council for School Education, alongside serving overseas clients with software development, application maintenance, testing and technical support.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Software & E-Governance Services:** Labour Department Management System (LDMS), software export services for overseas clients
- **Learning Solutions:** ICT school infrastructure & satellite-based computer education (525/53/398/412 school ICT projects, 301 BRC project, RSLDC project)
- **Media Services:** JAN TV (FTA channel), JAN TV Plus (pay channel)
- **Wind Power Generation:** wind power generation
- **Hospitality:** Hotel Ranavilas Palace, Jaipur
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- CSL Infomedia Private Limited — subsidiary: Material wholly owned subsidiary (100% shareholding), acquired 13 November 2010; related-party transactions include leasing/renting of Company property and service agreements for engagement/deputation of Compucom employees at government school ICT projects.
- Rishab Infotech Private Limited — related party: Entity belonging to the Promoter/promoter group; related-party transaction for leasing/renting of Company property.
business.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)

business.body:
- Decades of experience executing large-scale ICT and e-Governance projects for Government of Rajasthan departments, positioning the Company for future Government/institutional digital-education and public-digital-infrastructure initiatives
- Empanelment of subsidiary's JAN TV with DIPR (Government of Rajasthan) and CBC (Government of India, formerly DAVP) for Government advertising assignments, and multi-platform distribution (Tata Play, Airtel Digital TV, JioTV, MX Player, Dailyhunt, YouTube Live)
- Existing land bank enabling diversification into new consumer segments and industry verticals (hospitality, cold-chain/food processing) alongside the core ICT business
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Leverage the Company's existing land bank to sustain a steady rate of diversification into new consumer segments and industry verticals
- Build a more integrated and self-sustaining supply chain for the hospitality business, including planned backward integration with a nearby cold-chain and food-processing project
- Strengthen international presence in software exports/IT services as global technology spending gradually recovers, after recent moderation in overseas demand
- Strengthen JAN TV/JAN TV Plus regional presence (including its Uttar Pradesh bureau office) and pursue expanded government and commercial advertising outreach across additional states
- Explore strategic collaborations with reputed hospitality brands and service partners to augment Hotel Ranavilas Palace's market presence
- Leverage decades of experience in large-scale ICT/e-Governance execution to participate in future Government and institutional digital-education and public-digital-infrastructure initiatives
- The Board has proposed a final dividend of 12.50% (Rs. 0.25 per equity share) for the financial year ended 31 March 2026, subject to shareholder approval at the 32nd AGM.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's principal expansion project in FY2025-26 was Hotel Ranavilas Palace, Jaipur, which has now been completed and commenced full-fledged commercial operations; the year's higher capital expenditure and cash outflow was primarily on account of construction, fit-outs, interior works and other capital works for this hotel, which management expects to augment the Company's asset base, enhance operational capacity and contribute to future growth and revenue. On the wind-power side, the Company divested its two Sikar, Rajasthan wind plants (0.6 MW each) during the year for a total consideration of Rs. 53.57 lakhs (a loss of Rs. 1.43 lakhs), after their Power Purchase Agreements expired in December 2024 and the revised tariff was not commercially remunerative; the Company now operates a single 0.8 MW wind plant at Krishna District, Andhra Pradesh, whose operation and maintenance is managed by Wind World India Limited. In the Learning Solutions segment, the Company continues to execute five Government ICT/e-Governance school-infrastructure PPP projects (525, 53, 398, 412 schools and 301 BRCs) under multi-year (5-year) on-site warranty contracts, and states it has 'massive plans' to capture Indian education-expenditure opportunities through Government-promoted PPP models, planning to leverage in-house software development and satellite-based technology for expansion into schools and the coaching business.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian technology industry (IT services, BPM, engineering R&D, software products, hardware, emerging digital tech) is projected to grow 6.1% to ~US$315 billion in FY2025-26 per NASSCOM, driven by digital transformation, cloud computing, AI and Global Capability Centres
- AI-related revenues for Indian technology services companies are expected to reach ~US$10-12 billion in FY2025-26, supported by rising enterprise adoption of generative AI, automation, cloud-native platforms and digital engineering
- Sustained Government investment in digital governance and ICT infrastructure via MeitY and the Government of Rajasthan is expected to continue benefiting the Company's e-Governance project pipeline
- NEP 2020 and related digital-education initiatives (PM SHRI Schools, Digital India, DIKSHA, SWAYAM, PM eVIDYA, NDEAR) are accelerating adoption of digital learning and smart classrooms, supporting demand for the Company's ICT school-infrastructure offerings
- India's hospitality sector showed strong post-pandemic resilience in CY2025 (nationwide occupancy ~63-65%, rising ADR/RevPAR per HVS ANAROCK and Horwath HTL), supporting the outlook for the newly operational Hotel Ranavilas Palace, Jaipur
- International/overseas software services demand experienced moderation in recent periods due to global macroeconomic conditions, with gradual recovery expected as global technology spending improves
- India's wind-power installed capacity (~56.09 GW as of 31 March 2026) reflects continued government emphasis on clean-energy transition, though the Company's own wind portfolio has been reduced to a single 0.8 MW operating plant after divesting the Jaisalmer and Sikar sites
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
